dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Welcome to the WKU Talent Show! I'm going to ask each of you: what can you do? Kamila, let's start with you.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Hi everyone! My name is Kamila. I can play the dombra — I can play about twenty traditional Kazakh songs.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Fantastic! Can you also sing while you play?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Yes, I can sing a little! But I can't sing very well. I'm much better at playing than singing.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: That's wonderful! Now, Amir — what can you do?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I can do a live coding performance! I can build a working website on stage in fifteen minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: That's very unusual for a talent show! Can everyone in the audience understand coding?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Ha! Probably not. But I can also do magic tricks with a Rubik's cube — I can solve it in under two minutes!

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Impressive! Zhibek, what about you? What can you do?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I can dance! I can perform three different traditional Kazakh dances. I can also do gymnastics — I can do a backflip on stage.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: A backflip! Can you do it right now?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Of course I can! Watch this —

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Oh wow! That was incredible! And finally — Rustam, what can you do for our talent show?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I can juggle three footballs at the same time! And I can also do freestyle football tricks — I can balance the ball on my head for thirty seconds.

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Can you juggle and do tricks at the same time?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Yes, I can! I practise every morning. I can't sing or dance, but I can make a football do anything!

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.text: Amazing! So we have a dombra player, a tech wizard, a dancer, and a football freestyler. This is going to be the best WKU Talent Show ever!

questions.hint: can + not = can't / cannot. No 'to', no double 'n'.

questions.text: ___ Amir solve a Rubik's cube? — Yes, he can.
"She can dances beautifully." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: After can → bare infinitive. Not "dances" — just "dance".

questions.text: "He can't to juggle." is correct English.
questions.hint: Never use 'to' after can/can't. → He can't juggle.
